standard.title: Method for Calculation of Bulk Quantities of Petroleum and Liquid Petroleum Products (पेट्रोलियम और तरल पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों की थोक मात्रा की गणना की विधि)
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the standardized procedures, mathematical equations, temperature correction factors, and density-conversion coefficients used to calculate the bulk quantities (volumes and weights) of petroleum and liquid petroleum products stored in large bulk carrier tanks, stationary vertical storage tanks, or ship holds. It unifies calculation methods to provide the maximum possible accuracy in final calculated quantities compatible with the precision of physical measurements.

version.current_version: First Edition, June 1961 (Reaffirmed 2024, previous reaffirmations in 2002, 2013, 2018)
supersedes: None (Developed as a new standalone code to standardize bulk liquid petroleum calculations across the Indian oil and chemical sector)

relationships.description: Uses IS 1519 (Part I) : 1961 as a normative reference for requirements relevant to this standard.
References IS 1448 (Part I) : 1960 (P:16) for methods used to test the products or properties covered by this standard.
References IS 2 : 1960 (or IS 2 : 2022) for rules on rounding numerical values and reported measurements.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. However, under state distribution and legal metrology rules, central university petroleum research labs, oil public sector undertakings (PSUs), and customs calibration systems, newly designed fuel terminal systems are audited and verified to comply with the bulk density and temperature correction coefficients specified under IS 2164.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, densities, temperatures, and volumes must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The calculation method is explicitly optimized to ensure maximum possible accuracy in the final calculated quantities compatible with the precision of the physical measurements, utilizing standard calibration tables.
Accepted oil temperature must be substantially correct and obtained in accordance with the standard guidelines and precautions laid down in IS 1519 (Part I) : 1961.
All product densities must be determined strictly in accordance with standard hydrometer or pycnometer test methods laid down in P:16 of IS 1448 (Part I) : 1960.

Appendix E prescribes the volume correction coefficients per °C of petroleum products, to be used only for blends of petroleum with non-petroleum products based on standard density at 15°C (kg/l) (e.g. 0.5994 to 0.6022 kg/l uses 0.00173; 0.7416 to 0.7468 kg/l uses 0.00110; 1.0753 to 1.1249 kg/l uses 0.00058).

Appendix F defines standard coefficients for organic chemicals and solvents per °C (e.g. Benzene: 0.00124; Toluole: 0.00104; Xylole: 0.00100; Creosote oil: 0.00073; Coal tar: 0.00054; Methyl alcohol: 0.00118; Ethyl alcohol: 0.00108).
